name: Nepal
headline: Nepal: +4.4% growth in 2025, 4.1% inflation, debt 47% of GDP
sections: Nepal is a $45.5 billion economy (2025), the world's 103rd-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +4.4% in 2025, faster than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $6,175 at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 5.0% of GDP (2025).
Consumer prices rose 4.1% in 2025, above typical targets, down from 6.4% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 10.5% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 20.6% (2025).
Gross government debt is 47% of GDP (2025), a moderate level that has risen from 43% in 2020. The general government balance is −1.8% of GDP (2025).
The current account balance is +6.6% of GDP (2025), a large surplus. Trade equals 43% of GDP (2025), a relatively closed economy. Net FDI inflows were 0.1% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 48% of GDP by 2031, broadly stable from today's level. Life expectancy is 70.6 years (2024). Population: 29.6 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
